you will pot: from the children exposed in pots. Therefore Sophocles said 'to pot' for 'to kill' in Priam, and Aeschylus in Laius (fr. 120), and Pherecrates. "But Aeschylus must be thought to have said this word about Oedipus, whom Laius ordered to be exposed as a newborn."

Strangely said where the scholiast explains τῷ τόπῳ ἐκείνῳ [that place], i.e. the aged body. Wrongly in one copy ἐνὶ χώρᾳ [in one place], which should have been said as ἐν χώρᾳ [in a place]. That ἔvi [in one] is correctly read is shown by a similar passage Suppl. 749 γυνὴ μονωθεῖσ᾽ οὐδέν· οὐκ ἔνεστ᾽ ῎Αρης [a woman left alone is nothing; there is no Ares in her].
